creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Kan's server holds one active project shared by every browser tab, and the omnibar's board switcher (Cmd+P) changes it via `POST /api/v1/switch`. When the newly active project has no boards, `App.tsx` renders the "No boards found" screen and returns early (web/src/App.tsx:580), before `<Omnibar>` ever mounts. Cmd+P still calls `omnibar.open('boards')`, but there's nothing on screen to open, so the shortcut looks dead and there's no way back to a project that has boards.

I hit this on a beagle-served instance: its active project had switched to a repo that's registered in `~/.config/kan/config.toml` but was never `kan init`'d, leaving it with an empty board list and no visible way to switch away. Recovering meant restarting the server process, which re-runs project discovery from its working directory.

Worth deciding between two fixes, since they solve different parts of the trap:

- Keep the omnibar reachable even at zero boards, so Cmd+P still opens a way to pick another project.
- Put a project switcher directly on the "No boards found" screen, so recovery doesn't depend on remembering the hotkey.
title: cmd+p board switcher is unreachable once the active project has zero boards
